topic.angle: Tambora erupts, 1816 is freezing, and Frankenstein is born

panels.text: April 1815. Mount Tambora, on an island in Indonesia, erupts. It is the most powerful eruption in recorded history.
Ash and sulfur gases spread through the atmosphere and dim the sunlight. By 1816 Europe and North America are cold all summer.
Harvests fail and food prices jump. People call 1816 the Year Without a Summer.
The twist: at Villa Diodati in Switzerland, a group of friends is stuck indoors by the gloomy weather. They challenge each other to write ghost stories, and young Mary Shelley begins Frankenstein.

probes.question: Which volcano's 1815 eruption helped cause the Year Without a Summer?
True or false: Mary Shelley began writing Frankenstein during that cold, gloomy summer of 1816.

image_brief.show: Mount Tambora's caldera, or a stormy 19th-century landscape painting

claims.claim: Mount Tambora, on an island in Indonesia, erupted in April 1815
claims.quote: reached a violent climax on 10 April 1815

claims.claim: It is the most powerful eruption in recorded history
claims.quote: the most powerful volcanic eruption in recorded human history

claims.claim: Ash and sulfur gases dimmed sunlight
claims.quote: reflected significant amounts of solar radiation
claims.note: Ash/sulfur dioxide reaching the stratosphere also supported by the same page.

claims.claim: By 1816 Europe and North America were cold and wet all summer
claims.note: Europe cold/wet supported; North America supported as cold (June frost/snow), 'wet' not explicit for N. America; 'all summer' loose.

claims.claim: Harvests failed and food prices jumped
claims.quote: crop failures in New England, Canada, and parts of Europe caused food prices to rise sharply

claims.claim: 1816 called the Year Without a Summer
claims.quote: known as the "Year Without a Summer"

claims.claim: Friends near Lake Geneva were stuck indoors and challenged each other to write ghost stories
claims.note: Villa Diodati / ghost stories supported; 'Lake Geneva' only appears in a reference title ('Lake Geneva as Shelley and Byron Knew It'), not body text.

claims.claim: Mary Shelley was 18 when she began Frankenstein
claims.note: Fetched article says she wrote Frankenstein from this contest but does not state her age. Suggest dropping age or citing a source that gives it.

claims.claim: Probe: Tambora 1815 helped cause the Year Without a Summer
claims.quote: Cooling in the Northern Hemisphere in 1816, known as the "Year Without a Summer"

claims.claim: Probe: Shelley began Frankenstein in summer 1816
claims.quote: led Mary Shelley to write Frankenstein

claims.claim: Probe distractors Vesuvius/Krakatoa/St. Helens are wrong
claims.note: Not covered by fetched sources; trivially fine since Tambora is stated as the cause.
